class.name: Foliage3D
class.brief_description: Grass, trees, rocks and props growing on a [Terrain3D].
class.description: Draws the grass and objects held in a [FoliageData] on the [Terrain3D] at [member terrain_path], normally its parent. Paint them from the Terrain dock with the terrain or the foliage selected. Use [b]Add...[/b] in the Foliage list to bring in your own meshes and scenes, choosing whether each is painted as grass or placed as objects, or drag them in from the FileSystem dock. Grass is grown procedurally in square cells around the camera, within each type's [member FoliageType.visibility_range], a few cells a frame, and dropped again as the camera moves away. The painted density is all that is stored, so a field of grass costs almost nothing on disk. Blades shrink into the ground at the edge of the range instead of popping. Objects are kept individually, and built into cells of [member object_cell_size] metres: a [MultiMesh] per cell with collision from [member FoliageType.collision_shape], or an instance of [member FoliageType.scene] per object. They sit at the terrain's height, so sculpting under a tree carries the tree with the ground. While editing, grass grows around the camera of the 3D viewport last used. Objects with collision are included when a [NavigationRegion3D] bakes over the terrain, so monsters walk around trees rather than through them.

method.name: regenerate
method.description: Throws away every grass and object cell and builds them again on the next frame. Only needed after changing a [Mesh] or [PackedScene] a type uses from outside, since other changes are picked up automatically.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], objects whose type has a [member FoliageType.collision_shape] collide. Objects placed as scenes use their own collision whatever this says.
The physics layers the objects are in. See [member CollisionObject3D.collision_layer].
The physics layers the objects scan. See [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask].
The types of foliage and where each grows. The editor keeps it in its own compressed file beside the scene.
The most time, in milliseconds, spent growing grass in one frame. At least one cell is always grown. Raise it to fill in faster after a camera cut; lower it if growing grass causes hitches.
The size in metres of the square cells grass is grown and culled in.
The size in metres of the square cells objects are grouped into for drawing, culling and collision.
The [Terrain3D] the foliage grows on. Foliage positions are relative to that terrain, so moving the terrain moves its foliage with it.
